McLaren: McLaren has tweaked two key aero pieces for the weekend: the rear wing now features a new flap setting that straightens the car out on the long straights, giving a bit more top‑end speed, while the floor’s “furniture” has been reshaped to smooth the airflow underneath, boosting overall down‑force. In plain terms, the car should be quicker on the high‑speed sections and more stable through corners, which could translate into better lap times and a stronger fight for points this weekend.
Mercedes F1 Team: Mercedes has stripped away several small winglet pieces from the rear wing and trimmed the mirror‑wing on the front of the car to reduce drag for this circuit. The cleaner aerodynamics give the car a higher top‑speed on the straights, helping it stay competitive in qualifying and race pace. In short, the car is now sleeker and quicker where it matters most for this weekend’s layout.
Red Bull Racing: Red Bull have tweaked several key areas to make the car both sturdier and a bit more aero‑efficient for the weekend. The rear‑corner parts now have a reinforced link between the suspension and wheel bodywork, while a reshaped edge on the floor’s “bib” helps keep down‑force consistent under heavy loads. In addition, a sturdier exhaust‑tailpipe bracket and a refined front‑wing end‑plate vane improve reliability and clean up airflow, meaning the team can push harder without fearing mechanical gremlins.
Scuderia Ferrari: Ferrari has tweaked the underside and rear of the car to cut drag for this weekend’s high‑speed circuit – a slimmer front floor, a shorter mirror mount and the removal of a rear‑brake winglet all help the car slip through the air more cleanly. The new, slimmer tail winglet and trimmed side‑winglets further tighten the rear airflow, giving the team a boost in straight‑line speed and stability through the fast corners. In short, it’s all about shaving seconds off the lap by making the car “slimmer” where it matters most on this track.
Williams Racing: Williams has added a small vertical fence around the Halo for this circuit, which tightens airflow and helps keep the car stable at high speed. The front wing’s end‑plates have been made a bit narrower, giving a cleaner front‑end balance that improves turn‑in feel. Finally, a targeted trim on the floor cleans up the rear‑down‑force area, giving a little extra grip on the straights and through the fast corners. All three tweaks aim to boost stability and tyre performance for a stronger showing this weekend.
Racing Bulls / RB: Racing Bulls has fitted a circuit‑specific rear‑wing assembly that lets them fine‑tune drag more precisely, giving a better balance between straight‑line speed and corner grip for this track’s unique layout. They’ve also moved the exhaust tailpipe and reshaped its bracket to smooth the airflow, which should boost rear‑end stability and make the car feel more planted out of the fast corners. Together, these tweaks aim to shave off lap times and improve tyre wear over the weekend.
Aston Martin: Aston Martin has tweaked the front suspension’s outer covering, streamlining the airflow around that corner of the car, and reshaped the floor section just ahead of the rear tyre. The result is a cleaner aerodynamic “tunnel” that gives a bit more grip and stability when pushing hard through high‑speed corners. Those small but focused changes should translate into quicker lap times and better tyre wear over the weekend’s sprint and main race.
Haas F1 Team: Haas has given the car a quick aerodynamic makeover, adding a new front floor shape and a fresh side‑pod design with a slimmer roll‑hoop and a tweaked engine cover to boost down‑force and clean up airflow. The rear got a tidy‑up too—realigned suspension fairings and updated drum deflectors—to improve stability out of the fast corners. All these tweaks aim to give the car more grip and a steadier balance, so the drivers can push harder and fight more competitively this weekend.
Audi F1 Team: Audi F1 Team did not submit any updates for this event.
Alpine F1 Team: Alpine has tweaked the front‑wing endplates with a new footplate vane, giving the car a more stable front end and better grip through the corners. They’ve also stripped off the SM‑pod fairing on the rear wing, shaving off drag so the car can carry a little more speed on the straights. Together these changes should make the car feel more balanced out‑lap and give it a modest boost in overall pace for the weekend.
Cadillac: Cadillac has shifted the forward floor‑board stay outward and higher, straightening the airflow under the car for a cleaner, faster “tunnel” effect. They’ve also tacked a tiny vane onto the inner edge of the rear diffuser, nudging more air up the back to boost rear grip. Together, the tweaks should give the car steadier cornering and a little extra speed on the straights this weekend.
